hook: SCP-1437 is a bottomless pit in a desert that seems to open onto other universes, and every so often something shoots out of it. Read the first document carefully, because the rest of the article depends on noticing what changes. It is short, and the format does most of the work.
whyItMatters: It is a neat example of the file-as-story approach: one report repeats with variations, each copy coming from another world's version of the same organization. It plays with the idea that many Foundations might exist, some gentler and some far darker than ours, and leaves the comparing to the reader.
thingsToNotice:
Track the small details that drift between versions: the size of the hole, what the organization calls itself, how trespassers are treated, and the note attached to the gold disks.

The documents slide from familiar to corporate to theocratic to openly predatory, and each world misreads the others in revealing ways. The line describing whoever delivered each document says, briefly and abstractly, how that world treats people. The last version, run by unseen masters, quietly turns the hopeful reading of cooperation into something threatening.

related.note: Another look at a parallel world's Foundation, far bleaker than our own.
A different bottomless pit, played for a very different mood.
